# [CS042] Sensitive Data in Logs (sensitive-data-in-logs)

Passwords, tokens or personal data are written to logs.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-532](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/532.html) |
| **OWASP** | A09:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Logs are copied to many systems with weaker access control than the database. slog, zap, zerolog and log calls are checked for sensitive keys and for structs with sensitive fields; a type that defines its own log representation (slog.LogValuer, zapcore.ObjectMarshaler, zerolog.LogObjectMarshaler) is trusted.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
slog.Info("login", "user", req.Email, "password", req.Password)
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
slog.Info("login", "user", req.Email)
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [sensitive-data-in-logs]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    sensitive-data-in-logs: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore sensitive-data-in-logs -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** sensitive-data-in-logs
```
